look_here_first: Start with leaf architecture, not just leaflet count. Texas barberry usually has 5–9 leaflets, often with a reduced basal pair close to the rachis base, a dull gray-green reticulate surface, and a more open taller shrub form than agarita.

project_inclusion.range_basis: UT field work documents native B. swaseyi populations and hybrids in Hays, NW Travis, and Comal counties within the Edwards Plateau.

best_field_traits: basal leaflet pair often strongly reduced
more open less rounded shrub habit
yellow spring flowers and variable pale-to-reddish fruits
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Agarita is typically trifoliolate and denser. Hybrids commonly have 5–7 leaflets but lack the distinctive reduced basal leaflet pair of true B. swaseyi; use leaflet structure, bracts, and surface texture together.
